title: Cannabis Co-use and endocannabinoid system modulation in tobacco use disorder
title_zh: 大麻共用与烟草使用障碍中内源性大麻素系统调节
abstract: Tobacco use disorder (TUD) remains a leading cause of preventable mortality, and existing pharmacotherapies yield 12-month abstinence rates below 30%. As cannabis legalization expands, approximately 18-22% of people who use tobacco report concurrent cannabis use, yet the impact of co-use on cessation outcomes and the therapeutic potential of endocannabinoid system (ECS) modulation remain unclear. We conducted a translational systematic review and meta-analysis following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, searching Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, APA PsycInfo, and Web of Science through January 2026 (PROSPERO: CRD420250652724). Three study categories were eligible: observational studies of cannabis co-use and cessation outcomes; preclinical studies of cannabinoid modulators on nicotine-related behaviors; and human experimental studies of ECS-targeted interventions. Of 4869 records screened, 52 studies met inclusion criteria. Meta-analysis of 18 observational studies (N = 229,034) revealed that cannabis use was associated with 25% lower odds of achieving tobacco cessation (OR=0.75; 95% CI: 0.67-0.83; p < 0.0001; I²=81.1%). Preclinical evidence (15 studies) demonstrated that cannabinoid type-1 receptor (CB1R) antagonists robustly reduced nicotine self-administration and reinstatement, while cannabidiol (CBD) attenuated both nicotine intake and withdrawal without affecting food reinforcement. Clinical translation of CB1R inverse agonists failed due to psychiatric adverse effects, but CBD showed promise by reducing cigarette consumption by 40%, reversing attentional bias to smoking cues, and alleviating withdrawal severity. These findings distinguish naturalistic cannabis exposure from potentially beneficial targeted ECS modulation, and support CBD as a promising candidate for adequately powered tobacco cessation trials.
abstract_zh: 烟草使用障碍（TUD）仍是可预防死亡的主要原因，现有药物治疗的12个月戒烟率低于30%。随着大麻合法化的扩大，约18-22%的烟草使用者报告同时使用大麻，但共用对戒烟结果的影响以及内源性大麻素系统（ECS）调节的治疗潜力尚不清楚。我们按照PRISMA 2020指南进行转化性系统综述和荟萃分析，检索Ovid MEDLINE、Embase、APA PsycInfo和Web of Science，截止2026年1月（PROSPERO: CRD420250652724）。共有三类研究符合纳入标准：观察性研究探讨大麻共用与戒烟结果；前临床研究评估大麻素调节剂对尼古丁相关行为的影响；以及人类实验研究ECS靶向干预。筛选4869条记录后，52项研究符合纳入条件。对18项观察性研究（N=229,034）的荟萃分析显示，大麻使用与烟草戒烟的可能性降低25%相关（OR=0.75；95% CI: 0.67-0.83；p<0.0001；I²=81.1%）。前临床证据（15项研究）表明，CB1受体（CB1R）拮抗剂显著降低尼古丁自给自足和复发，而大麻二酚（CBD）则在不影响食物强化的情况下，抑制尼古丁摄入和戒断。CB1R逆激动剂的临床转化因精神不良反应失败，但CBD显示出潜力，能将香烟消费减少40%，逆转对吸烟线索的注意偏差，并减轻戒断严重程度。这些发现区分了自然大麻暴露与潜在有益的靶向ECS调节，并支持CBD作为足够样本量的烟草戒烟试验的有前景候选者。
